newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Burundi sanction talks end in Zambian capital.
newsitem.headline: Burundi sanction talks end in Zambian capital.

text.p: Two-day talks by the regional Sanctions Co-ordinating Committee on Burundi ended in Lusaka on Friday but it was unclear whether any decision had been made altering the sanctions on the east African country.
"It is all hush-hush. No statements will be made," said a foreign affairs official in the Zambian capital.

The meeting -- attended by representatives from Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, Zaire and Zambia -- was called to review conditions for lifting the sanctions, imposed last year after a military coup.
The sanctions committee has set three conditions for the lifting of sanctions against Burundi: the unbanning of political parties, the restoration of parliament and a return to constitutional rule.
The Lusaka meeting, which was initially scheduled to end on Thursday, was the fourth to be held by the committee since it was formed in August.
Burundi's military ruler Major Pierre Buyoya seized power from the civilian government on July 25 last year.
